title: xfeeds: an independence-aware public threat intelligence feed
description:
xfeeds is a self-updating, open threat intelligence pipeline that collects, normalizes, enriches, scores, filters, and publishes malicious-IP indicators in interoperable formats (CSV, JSON, STIX 2.1, MISP, and firewall rule sets). A scheduled six-hour GitHub Actions pipeline regenerates every feed and a reader-facing dashboard served over GitHub Pages.

Most public blocklists mirror or re-derive one another, so naive aggregation manufactures false confidence. xfeeds models that dependency explicitly:

  • Independence classes. Sources are grouped into families, and only the strongest contribution within a family counts toward corroboration, so mirrored lists cannot vote twice.
  • Freshness gating. Successful fetches do not establish evidence freshness. Dormant observations may corroborate fresh evidence but cannot independently promote an indicator.
  • Redistribution-aware tiering. Restricted sources may raise confidence without appearing in published records. Separate non-commercial and clean-provenance feed tiers carry distinct redistribution promises, each with a generated licence-and-credit manifest.
  • Conservative admission. Indicators observed by only a single independent sensor network are discarded. Benign-scanner evidence caps confidence rather than deleting records, preserving the consumer's policy choice.

Design decisions, source methodology, and licence research are recorded in the repository under docs/.
